record.original_question: Determine whether the cubic Diophantine equation 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1 has an integer solution.

evidence.quote: The shortest cubic equation for which Problem 6 is open is the equation 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1 (39) of length l = 9 + log2 21 ~= 13.4.
Problem 6. Given a Diophantine equation, determine whether it has an integer solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Decide whether there exist integers $x, y, z \in \mathbb{Z}$ satisfying the Diophantine equation
$$7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1.$$
That is, determine whether this equation admits an integer solution, or prove that no such solution exists.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the specific equation 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1 was found in web searches. It is referenced as the shortest cubic Diophantine equation for which the decidability question of integer solvability remains unresolved, and no evidence indicates it has since been solved.
